Predictions from a fitted model

predict.cv.bregsurv.Rd

Predictions from a fitted model

Usage

# S3 method for class 'cv.bregsurv'
predict(
  object,
  newz,
  stratum = NULL,
  type = c("lp", "hazard", "survival"),
  times = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'bregsurv'
predict(
  object,
  newz,
  stratum = NULL,
  type = c("lp", "hazard", "survival"),
  times = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A cv.bregsurv or bregsurv fit.

newz

Covariates of new subjects, with the target's column names.

stratum

Strata of the new subjects, when the target was stratified.

type

What to predict:

  • "lp": the risk score (the linear predictor \(z^\top\beta\), or the network output) of a Cox or nested case-control target;

  • "hazard": the interval hazards of a discrete-time target, one column per interval;

  • "survival": survival probabilities: at the end of each interval for a discrete-time target, or at times for a Cox target (with the Breslow baseline hazard of the training data).

times

Times at which to evaluate survival for a Cox target.

...

Unused.

Value

A vector ("lp") or a matrix with one row per new subject.

Examples

data(ExampleData_lowdim)
tr <- ExampleData_lowdim$train; te <- ExampleData_lowdim$test
fit <- cv.bregsurv(target_cox(tr$time, tr$status, tr$z),
                   release_coef(ExampleData_lowdim$beta_external_fair), divergence = "kl")
head(predict(fit, te$z))
#>         1         2         3         4         5         6 
#> 1.5541437 0.8073051 2.3118085 1.8861394 1.3005752 1.7741216 
predict(fit, te$z[1:3, ], type = "survival", times = c(1, 2, 3))
#>             t=1        t=2        t=3
#> [1,] 0.27815967 0.27815967 0.27815967
#> [2,] 0.54534579 0.54534579 0.54534579
#> [3,] 0.06524075 0.06524075 0.06524075
